title: fix(providers): pickers and defaults offer 35 models their providers have retired
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: picking one of 35 bundled models fails every turn because the provider has retired it (404 / 410 "end of life" / "archived"), and new Cerebras setups default to an archived model.

## User Impact

User impact: model pickers, onboarding defaults, and media defaults stop offering models the provider no longer serves. New Cerebras setups default to `cerebras/gpt-oss-120b` instead of the archived `gemma-4-31b`; Together defaults to GLM 5.2; DeepInfra image understanding falls back to Kimi K2.6; OpenCode image understanding defaults to MiniMax M3. Configs that pin a removed id are not rewritten (no Doctor rewrites); those turns already fail at the provider today.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each removed row was proven retired live with a real API key on 2026-10-13: the id is absent from the provider's `GET /models` listing **and** a 1-token completion against the catalog `baseUrl` failed. Rows that were merely unlisted but still served (aliases, access-gated models, region-dependent `qwen` rows) were left alone. Doctor name-table rewrites were deliberately not added (see #169473). This complements #167855, which marks dead rows `deprecated` only in the hosted catalog bundle and only for providers with a keyless `/models`; this PR prunes the bundled manifests themselves, including key-gated providers (Cerebras, Groq, Fireworks, Together, Qwen Token Plan) that #167855 cannot see.

| provider | removed | live result |
|---|---|---|
| cerebras | zai-glm-4.7, gemma-4-31b | 404 `model_archived` |
| groq | groq/compound, groq/compound-mini, llama-3.1-8b-instant, llama-3.3-70b-versatile | 404 `model_not_found` |
| chutes | Kimi-K2.5-TEE, MiniMax-M2.5-TEE | 404 |
| fireworks | kimi-k2p6, kimi-k2p6-turbo | 404 not deployed |
| novita | deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash | 404 |
| nvidia | glm-5.2, glm-5.1, glm5, minimax-m3, minimax-m2.7, deepseek-v4-pro, qwen3.5-397b-a17b | 410 "reached its end of life" |
| nvidia | moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 | 404, unlisted |
| ollama-cloud | kimi-k2.5, deepseek-v4-flash(:0731, :preview), deepseek-v4-pro:preview, glm-5.1, qwen3.5(:397b) | 410 "was retired on …" |
| qwen-token-plan | qwen3-coder-next | 404 |
| opencode | gpt-5-nano | 403 "Model access is disabled", unlisted |
| together | Kimi-K2.6, DeepSeek-V4-Pro | no serverless deployment, unlisted |
| deepinfra | Kimi-K2.5, Kimi-K2.7-Code, Step-3.5-Flash, Step-3.7-Flash | unlisted; requests silently served by a different model |

## Evidence

- Live catalog sweep with real keys across 28 providers: `/models` diff plus a real completion per candidate (results in the table).
- Live gateway agent smoke (`src/gateway/gateway-models.profiles.live.test.ts`) on the new OpenCode image default `opencode/minimax-m3`: prompt, read tool, exec tool, and image probe all passed.
- Touched plugin tests, production + extension-test typechecks, generated config/manifest baselines, formatting, `git diff --check`.
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean, no findings.
- Local gap: `src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts` (only change: an NVIDIA Kimi fixture id) timed out at 42–54s on a host at load ~300; PR CI is the authority for it.

- Rebase refresh: head `f126d8028934deb91d71453b6193ff47b1004568` is rebased onto `be3f6264aa0fa3e15b25606640a441860b3b36ba`, including the inherited mock-export fix in #171916. Both PR commits are patch-identical (`git range-diff`); there were no conflicts or generated-file resolutions. `pnpm test extensions/qwen/onboard.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 9/9 after rebase (57.27s runner wall time, 30.90s Vitest duration). The stale eight-row Qwen expectation was corrected before this rebase and independently reviewed scoped-clean.
- Local rerun limit: a broader 14-file touched-plugin batch completed worker preparation but stalled without test results on a heavily loaded host. It was explicitly stopped with SIGTERM, not counted as passing, and fully drained before the focused rerun. Fresh-head PR CI supplies the broad proof; no timeouts or assertions were weakened.
- Review follow-up: the Together legacy normalizer and Groq Doctor name table noted by the inline review are unchanged by this PR; their targets already failed the live provider probes before catalog removal. Retargeting saved choices is a separate migration-policy change tracked by #169473, not a consequence of removing picker rows. This PR intentionally adds no name-table rewrites.
